# Job Planner

Run a small deterministic file-task plan and persist each result. Python 3.10+ and the standard library are sufficient.

`python3 job_planner.py samples/plan.json` runs three included jobs: line count, SHA-256 and CSV dimensions. It prints completed/failed counts and writes `.results/latest.json`. The plan refers to `samples/notes.txt` and `samples/sales.csv` inside the chosen root. Use `--root` to set that directory and `--output` for a relative report path. `samples/plan-dependencies.json` shows forward references, a failed branch with blocked downstream jobs, and an independent job still succeeding.

Supported operations are count-lines, sha256 and csv-summary. Jobs without dependencies run sequentially in plan order; results have no timestamps so identical inputs produce identical report content. Duplicate job names are rejected. Per-job file or operation errors are recorded and subsequent jobs continue. Exit codes are 0 when all jobs complete, 1 when any job fails or is blocked, and 2 for an invalid plan or report path.

A job may declare `"depends_on": [other job names]`; a missing key or empty list means no dependencies. Names match exactly and may point forward in the plan. The whole dependency graph is validated before anything runs: `depends_on` must be a list of nonblank names with no duplicates, and every name must exist, not be the job itself and not form a cycle. Any violation makes `run_plan` raise `ValueError`; the CLI prints its `{"error": ...}` JSON, returns 2 and leaves any existing report untouched.

On each pass the plan runs the earliest-in-plan pending job whose direct dependencies already have records; dependency-free jobs take part in the same choice. A job executes its operation only when every direct dependency `completed`. If any direct dependency is `failed` or `blocked`, the job does not read its input and is recorded with only `name`, `status: "blocked"` and `blocked_by` (every failing or blocked direct dependency, in `depends_on` order); blocked state propagates downstream and each task produces exactly one record. Results in the report are ordered by actual processing order. When at least one job has a nonempty `depends_on`, the CLI summary adds a `blocked` count (the `failed` count still covers operation failures only); plans without dependencies keep the original summary fields.

To run only part of a plan, pass `run_plan(root, jobs, output, targets=[...])` or repeat the CLI's `--only NAME` once per job. Each target is one exact job name (no case folding or trimming); the run covers the targets plus all their direct and indirect prerequisites — shared prerequisites run once and target order never changes execution order. The whole plan is still validated (names, dependencies, input path boundaries) before the scope is chosen, so errors in unselected branches reject the run. Jobs outside the scope are not read, produce no records and cannot affect the exit code; the report and the returned list contain only the jobs processed this run, and the CLI counts and the optional `blocked` field describe that same scope. An empty or non-list `targets`, non-string or blank entries, duplicates and unknown names all raise `ValueError` (CLI: `{"error": ...}` JSON, exit 2, no tasks run, existing report untouched). Omitting `targets`/`--only` runs the full plan exactly as before.

Report saving is atomic in every execution mode (`run_plan`, `run_retry`, `run_history_retry` and `run_changes`). The new report is fully serialized and UTF-8 encoded before the filesystem is touched: a report that cannot be encoded as one complete UTF-8 JSON document raises `ValueError`, and a filesystem error while creating the output directory, saving the content or replacing the output raises `OSError` — including when the output path already is a directory. Either failure happens after the tasks have run and leaves the pre-run output file byte-for-byte intact — or still absent when there was none — with no partial or extra files left behind (empty parent directories created for the attempt may remain); finished tasks are not undone and a failed save never turns their results into failures. Only a successful save means the new results have fully replaced the old ones, so a historical report that is also the output stays queryable after a failed save, and a legal in-root symlink output updates the resolved target while the link itself is kept. On a save failure the CLI prints only its `{"error": ...}` JSON and exits 2, without completion statistics. The saved file keeps the permissions a plain overwrite would have: on Unix an existing output's permission bits are preserved and a new file follows the process umask, while platforms without a file-descriptor permission interface (such as Windows) skip that step and follow their normal file semantics — a missing or unimplemented interface is not a permission denial and never fails the save, but a real denial (including a read-only target refusing replacement) surfaces as `OSError` like any other filesystem error.

To preview a retry from a previous run report, call `preview_retry(root, jobs, output, report)` or pass `--retry-preview REPORT` (optionally with `--root` and `--output`); `report` is a root-relative report path and may equal `output`. Every result whose `status` is `failed` or `blocked` becomes a retry target, in current plan order regardless of report record order, and the returned object is `{"targets": [...], "jobs": [...]}`. The jobs cover the targets and all their prerequisites — including prerequisites the report marked `completed`, since rerunning manually reprocesses them, and shared prerequisites appear once — with the same fields, order and `target`/`prerequisite` reasons as `preview_plan` with targets. The report may cover a partial run: unrecorded tasks join the preview only when they are needed prerequisites, and unrelated branches are omitted. With no failed or blocked records the result is `{"targets": [], "jobs": []}`. The whole plan and the output path are validated first, even for an empty retry range, including unselected branches. The report must be a UTF-8 JSON object whose `results` is a list of objects; each `name` must exactly match a current task without repeats and `status` must be `completed`, `failed` or `blocked` (other fields are ignored and an empty list is valid). The whole file is parsed as strict JSON, so a bare `NaN`, `Infinity` or `-Infinity` constant is rejected anywhere it appears — nested in a `result`, in an extra top-level field or an entry's extra field, and even when `results` is empty or no record would be retried — while the same words written as JSON strings are harmless; legal JSON numbers keep their previous parsing here (out-of-float-range exponents included). A missing, unreadable, non-UTF-8 or invalid-JSON report, wrong structure, unknown or duplicate names, illegal status, or a report path that is absolute or resolves (via symlinks) outside root all raise `ValueError`; the CLI prints `{"error": ...}` JSON and returns 2. `--retry-preview` cannot be combined with `--preview` or `--only`. A retry preview reads only the plan and the report: it never runs tasks, reads task inputs, creates directories or writes anything, success or failure leaves every existing file unchanged, and it does not promise the tasks would succeed (missing inputs, unknown operations and bad contents still preview). Ordinary runs remain driven solely by that run's results.

To execute a manual retry from a previous run report, call `run_retry(root, jobs, output, report)` or pass `--retry REPORT` (optionally with `--root` and `--output`). Target selection and scope are exactly the retry preview's: the report's `failed`/`blocked` tasks become targets in current plan order, the run covers them plus every direct and indirect prerequisite (including ones the report marked `completed` — they are re-executed), shared prerequisites run once, unrecorded tasks join only as required prerequisites of a partial report, and unrelated branches are neither read nor recorded. Execution order, failure records and `blocked_by` propagation are `run_plan`'s; file-read failures, unknown operations and invalid contents are recorded `failed`, independent branches keep running, and dependency decisions use only this run's results. The returned list and the report at `output` contain only this run's records — old records are never copied — and the CLI counts describe that same scope with the same exit codes as an ordinary run (0 when nothing failed or blocked, otherwise 1). `report` may equal `output`: targets are taken from the content read before the overwrite. With no retry targets `run_retry` returns `[]` without reading task inputs, creating directories or rewriting the report, and the CLI prints `{"completed":0,"failed":0}` and exits 0. The whole plan — names, dependencies, every input path and output protection, including unselected branches and an empty retry scope — is validated first; report validation is identical to `preview_retry`'s (missing, unreadable, non-UTF-8, invalid JSON — including a bare `NaN`/`Infinity`/`-Infinity` constant anywhere in the file, even in an ignored field or an empty results list — wrong structure, unknown/duplicate names or illegal status all raise `ValueError`; the same words inside strings are legal), so such a report never starts a run, and the CLI prints error-only JSON and exits 2 without running or changing files. Saving follows the atomic report-saving rule: an unencodable report raises `ValueError` and filesystem errors raise `OSError` (CLI: error-only JSON, exit 2) after tasks have run, leaving the pre-run output byte-for-byte intact — so with `report` equal to `output` the historical report stays queryable after a failed save — and executed tasks are not undone. `--retry` cannot be combined with `--only`, `--preview` or `--retry-preview`.

To compare two existing reports read-only and see whether tasks recovered or changed, call `compare_reports(root, jobs, output, before, after)` or pass `--compare BEFORE AFTER` (with the usual plan argument, `--root` and `--output`). It returns `{"jobs": [...]}` in current plan order listing every task recorded in at least one report; each entry has only `name`, `before`, `after` and `change`. A side with no record is `null`; a present side keeps only `status` plus its matching payload — `result` (an object) for `completed`, `error` (a string) for `failed`, `blocked_by` for `blocked`, the latter emitted in current dependency declaration order. `change` is `added` when only the after report records the task, `removed` when only before does, `changed` when the statuses or payloads differ (including a different failure message), otherwise `unchanged`; an unrecorded task is never treated as failed. Comparison ignores report record order and extra fields: numbers nested anywhere in `result` compare by the exact decimal value the report expresses, so `1`, `1.0` and `1e0` are equal and negative zero equals zero, while `0.10000000000000001` differs from `0.1`, `9007199254740993.0` from `9007199254740992.0`, `2e400` from `1e400` and `1e-400` from `0` (whereas `1e400` equals `10e399`), all without float precision loss even beyond the float range; otherwise JSON value equality applies — booleans differ from numbers, numbers differ from strings with the same digits, object key order is irrelevant and array order is significant; `blocked_by` compares as a set. Both reports are fully validated before any comparison is returned: long decimals and syntactically legal exponents outside float range are accepted, while `NaN`, `Infinity` and `-Infinity` reject the report even inside ignored extra fields (the same words inside strings are harmless). The returned sides keep the report's numbers as numbers preserving their value rather than strings or rounded floats, and the CLI prints them as legal JSON numbers (never `Infinity`); trailing zeros and exponent spelling are not preserved. The whole plan (including unrecorded branches), every input path and the output path are validated first, exactly like a run, and the CLI also protects the plan file. The reports follow the retry report rules (UTF-8 JSON object with a `results` list of objects, names matching the plan with no repeats and valid statuses; missing, unreadable, non-UTF-8, invalid-JSON, absolute or symlink-escaping paths all raise `ValueError`), and this entry point additionally requires the status payload to be present and well shaped: `result` must be an object, `error` a string, and `blocked_by` a nonempty, duplicate-free array naming only the job's declared direct dependencies. `--compare` cannot be combined with `--only`, `--preview`, `--retry-preview` or `--retry`; the CLI prints error-only JSON and exits 2 on any validation failure or option conflict, while a valid comparison exits 0 even when records are failed or blocked. A comparison is strictly read-only: it never runs tasks, reads task inputs, creates directories or writes files, and `before` and `after` may name the same file.

To understand from a single report why tasks failed or stayed blocked, call `explain_report(root, jobs, output, report)` or pass `--explain REPORT` (with the usual plan argument, `--root` and `--output`). It returns `{"jobs": [...]}` in current plan order containing only the tasks the report records as `failed` or `blocked`; each entry has only `name`, `status` and `causes`. A `failed` task has exactly one cause — itself, `status: "failed"` with the report's `error` string preserved verbatim. A `blocked` task is explained by following that report's `blocked_by` references level by level: reaching a `failed` record stops that branch on it as a terminal cause, reaching a `blocked` record expands that record's own `blocked_by`, and reaching a task with no record stops on an `{"name", "status": "unrecorded", "error": null}` cause. Only the report is traced — current file contents and other declared dependencies are never used to infer a cause — and if any `blocked_by` chain reaches a task the report records as `completed`, the whole explanation raises `ValueError`. Causes are de-duplicated by task name and emitted in current plan order, independently of report record order; the report may be partial, and an unrecorded task appears only when it is a trace endpoint, never as its own job. With no failed or blocked records the result is `{"jobs": []}`. Validation mirrors `compare_reports` exactly: the whole plan (including unrecorded branches), every input path and the output path are checked first, and the report must satisfy the same path, encoding, structure, name, status and strict payload rules (`result` object, `error` string, nonempty duplicate-free `blocked_by` naming only declared direct dependencies); extra fields are ignored. That includes rejecting a bare `NaN`/`Infinity`/`-Infinity` constant anywhere in the report — nested in a `result`, in an extra field or at top level, even with empty `results` — while the same words inside strings stay legal and an error string containing them is returned verbatim. `--explain` cannot be combined with `--only`, `--preview`, `--retry-preview`, `--retry` or `--compare`; the CLI prints error-only JSON and exits 2 on any validation failure or option conflict, while a valid explanation exits 0 even when it contains failures. An explanation is strictly read-only: it reads only the plan and the named report, never task inputs, and it never runs tasks, creates directories or writes files; `report` may equal `output`.

To query one task's record across several reports read-only, call `query_history(root, jobs, output, reports, targets=None)` or repeat the CLI's `--history REPORT` (with the usual plan argument, `--root`, `--output` and optional `--only NAME`). `reports` is a nonempty list of root-relative report paths; each entry must be a nonblank string and repeats are allowed. Reports are shown strictly in the order given — nothing is sorted by name or modification time and no other reports are scanned — so a repeated path yields a repeated, equal history position. It returns `{"jobs": [...]}` in current plan order; each entry has only `name` and `history`, a list as long as `reports` whose slots are `{"report": ..., "record": ...}` with `report` the path verbatim. A slot is `null` when that report has no record for the task (a missing record is never a failure and is never filled in from a neighbouring report); a present record keeps only `status` plus its matching payload with the same rules as `compare_reports` — `result` (an object) for `completed`, `error` (a string) for `failed`, and `blocked_by` for `blocked`, emitted in current dependency declaration order, with extra fields ignored. Numbers nested anywhere in a `completed` record's `result` keep the exact decimal value the report expresses, exactly as in `compare_reports`: the API returns them as numbers preserving their value (never rounded to float, collapsed to zero or infinity, or turned into strings — `0.10000000000000001`, `9007199254740993.0`, `1e400` and `1e-400` survive), the CLI prints them as legal JSON numbers (trailing zeros and exponent spelling are not preserved), and `NaN`, `Infinity` or `-Infinity` constants anywhere in a report — even in ignored extra fields — reject the query, while the same words inside strings are harmless. Without `--only` only tasks appearing in at least one report are listed, so all-empty reports give `{"jobs": []}`. With targets the listed tasks are exactly those named: the prerequisite closure is not expanded, target argument order never changes plan order, and a task no report ever records still appears with an all-`null` history as long as the name exists in the plan; illegal targets raise `ValueError` exactly as elsewhere. The whole plan (including unrecorded branches), every input path and the output path are validated first, and then every report is validated with the compare report's path, UTF-8, structure, name, status and strict payload rules — including records outside the `--only` scope and every later report in the list — so an absolute or symlink-escaping path, a missing/non-UTF-8/invalid-JSON report, a malformed payload, an empty or non-list `reports`, or a blank/non-string entry all raise `ValueError` with no partial history returned. `--history` cannot be combined with `--preview`, `--retry-preview`, `--retry`, `--compare` or `--explain`; the CLI prints error-only JSON and exits 2 on any validation failure or option conflict, while a valid query exits 0 even when records are failed or blocked. A history query is strictly read-only: it reads only the plan and the named reports, never task inputs, and it never runs tasks, creates directories or writes files; a report may equal `output`.

To preview a retry range from several historical reports ordered oldest to newest, call `preview_history_retry(root, jobs, output, reports, max_failures=None)` or repeat the CLI's `--history-retry REPORT` (with the usual plan argument, `--root` and `--output`). `reports` is a nonempty list of root-relative report paths; each entry must be a nonblank string and repeats keep separate positions. Reports are interpreted strictly in the order given — nothing is sorted by name or modification time and no other reports are scanned — so a repeated path yields a separate, later position. Each task is judged by the last report (highest index) containing a record of it: a newer report that omits the task never clears an older status. A task becomes a retry target exactly when its latest record is `failed` or `blocked`, and targets appear in current plan order regardless of report record order; a task whose latest record is `completed`, or that no report ever records, is not a target. The returned object has exactly `targets`, `jobs` and `sources`. `jobs` cover the targets and every direct and indirect prerequisite — prerequisites that completed in history or were never recorded are included too, shared prerequisites appear once and unrelated branches are omitted — with the same fields, processing order and `target`/`prerequisite` reasons as `preview_plan` with those targets. `sources` corresponds to `targets` one to one and in the same order; each entry has only `name` (the target), `status` (its latest status), `report` (the source path verbatim) and `index` (that report's zero-based position in `reports`). With no targets the result is `{"targets": [], "jobs": [], "sources": []}`. The history only selects the range: the new run's dependency decisions still use only that run's own results, never inherited records. The whole plan (including unselected branches), every input path and the output path are validated first, exactly like a run, and then every report is fully validated with the path, UTF-8, structure, name, status and strict payload rules of `query_history` — including tasks that are not selected, older records a newer report overrides and every later report in the list — so an absolute or symlink-escaping path, a missing/non-UTF-8/invalid-JSON report, a malformed payload, an empty or non-list `reports`, or a blank/non-string entry all raise `ValueError` with no partial result returned. The whole file is strict JSON: a bare `NaN`, `Infinity` or `-Infinity` constant rejects any report even inside an ignored extra field, while the same words inside strings and syntactically legal JSON numbers (out-of-float-range exponents included) are accepted. `--history-retry` cannot be combined with `--only`, `--record-reasons` or any execution, preview or report-query option (`--preview`, `--retry-preview`, `--retry`, `--compare`, `--explain`, `--history`, `--execution`, `--changed`, `--run-changed`); the CLI prints error-only JSON and exits 2 on any validation failure or option conflict, while a valid preview prints the object and exits 0 even when records are failed or blocked. The preview is strictly read-only: it reads only the plan and the named reports (a report may equal `output`), never task inputs, and it never runs tasks, creates directories or writes files.

An optional failure limit narrows the history retry preview's range: pass `max_failures=N` to `preview_history_retry` or add the CLI's `--max-failures N` (a positive integer, valid only together with `--history-retry`). With the limit off (`None`, or the flag absent) the selection and the returned object are exactly as above. With it on, every task counts its `failed` records since its latest `completed` record, walking the reports in the given order: `completed` resets the count to zero, `blocked` and missing records neither increment nor reset it, and a repeated report path counts once per position. The candidates are still the tasks whose latest record is `failed` or `blocked`, but a candidate is excluded when its own count or the count of any direct or indirect prerequisite has reached the limit. The result then carries a fourth array — `{"targets": [...], "jobs": [...], "sources": [...], "excluded": [...]}` — where `targets`, `jobs` and `sources` describe only the retained candidates exactly as before and each `excluded` entry has only `name` (the excluded candidate), `failures` (its own count) and `limited_by` (every task at the limit that caused the exclusion — the candidate itself included when it qualifies — in plan order without repeats). `targets`, `excluded` and `limited_by` follow plan order; with no candidates all four arrays are empty, and when every candidate is excluded only `excluded` is non-empty. `max_failures` must be `None` or a positive, non-boolean integer — any other value raises `ValueError` (CLI: error-only JSON, exit 2, no partial preview), as does `--max-failures` without `--history-retry` or combined with any other mode option. Plan and report validation are unchanged: the whole plan and every report are still fully validated, including unselected branches and overridden records, and the preview stays strictly read-only. The limit only filters this preview; `run_history_retry` and every other entry point are unchanged.

To execute the retry range selected from several historical reports, call `run_history_retry(root, jobs, output, reports, record_reasons=False)` or repeat the CLI's `--run-history-retry REPORT` (with the usual plan argument, `--root` and `--output`). The range and scope are exactly `preview_history_retry`'s: `reports` is a nonempty list of nonblank root-relative paths interpreted oldest to newest in the order given (repeats keep separate positions, nothing is sorted or scanned), each task is judged by the last report recording it — a later report missing the task never clears an older status — and tasks whose latest record is `failed` or `blocked` become targets in current plan order. The run covers the targets plus every direct and indirect prerequisite — completed or never-recorded prerequisites are re-executed, shared prerequisites run once — and unrelated branches are neither read nor recorded. Execution order, failure records and `blocked_by` propagation are `run_plan`'s, judged on this run's results only: input read failures, unknown operations and invalid contents are recorded `failed`, independent branches keep running and blocked tasks never read their input. The returned list and the report at `output` contain only this run's records under `results` — old records are never copied — and the CLI counts describe that same scope with the usual summary fields and exit codes (0 when nothing failed or blocked, otherwise 1). A report path may equal `output` or name the same file another way: the range is chosen from all the historical content read before the overwrite. With no targets `run_history_retry` returns `[]` without reading task inputs, creating directories or rewriting the report, and the CLI prints `{"completed":0,"failed":0}` and exits 0. The whole plan — names, dependencies, every input path and output protection, including unselected branches and an empty scope — is validated first, and then every report is fully validated under `preview_history_retry`'s path, UTF-8, structure, name, status and strict payload rules, including out-of-scope and overridden older records; any violation raises `ValueError` (CLI: error-only JSON, exit 2) before anything runs or changes. Saving follows the atomic report-saving rule: an unencodable report raises `ValueError` and filesystem errors raise `OSError` (CLI: error-only JSON, exit 2) after tasks have run, leaving the pre-run output byte-for-byte intact — so a historical report aliasing `output` stays queryable after a failed save — and executed tasks are not undone. With `record_reasons=True` and at least one target the report gains the top-level `execution` object with `mode` `"retry"` and `targets`/`jobs` exactly matching `preview_history_retry` (`sources` is not recorded), readable through `query_execution`; `record_reasons` must be a plain boolean. `--run-history-retry` combines only with `--root`, `--output` and `--record-reasons`; any execution, preview or query option alongside it conflicts (error-only JSON, exit 2).

To preview which tasks a set of changed input files would affect, call `preview_changes(root, jobs, output, changed_inputs)` or repeat the CLI's `--changed PATH` (with the usual plan argument, `--root` and `--output`). `changed_inputs` is a list of root-relative path strings; an empty list is allowed, every entry must be a nonblank string, and each path is resolved exactly like a plan input path — absolute paths and paths resolving (via symlinks) outside root raise `ValueError`, even when they would match nothing. Paths resolving to the same file are merged and argument order never changes the result. Matching uses resolved paths only: files need not exist and are never read, and a legal path matching no task input simply produces no targets. The result is `{"targets": [...], "jobs": [...]}`: targets are the tasks whose resolved input path was directly changed plus every task downstream of them along declared dependencies, each once, in original plan order; jobs cover the targets and all their prerequisites, each once, in the usual preview processing order with the same `depends_on`, `reason` (`target`/`prerequisite`) and `required_by` semantics as `preview_plan` with targets, plus a `triggered_by` field listing the directly changed tasks that can reach the job along dependency edges, in original plan order — a directly changed task lists itself, and jobs included only as prerequisites get `[]`. With no changed inputs or no matching task the result is `{"targets": [], "jobs": []}`. The whole plan, every input path and the output path are validated exactly like a run before the scope is chosen, even for an empty result; any violation or an illegal `changed_inputs` raises `ValueError`, and the CLI prints `{"error": ...}` JSON and exits 2 while a valid preview prints the object and exits 0. `--changed` cannot be combined with `--only`, `--preview`, `--retry-preview`, `--retry`, `--compare`, `--explain` or `--history`. A change preview is strictly read-only: it reads only the plan, never task inputs, old reports or file contents, and it never runs tasks, creates directories or writes files.

To execute the tasks affected by a set of changed input files, call `run_changes(root, jobs, output, changed_inputs)` or repeat the CLI's `--run-changed PATH` (with the usual plan argument, `--root` and `--output`). The scope is exactly what `preview_changes` would show for the same paths: the tasks whose resolved input path was directly changed plus every downstream dependent become targets in plan order, the run covers them plus every direct and indirect prerequisite, and shared prerequisites run once. `changed_inputs` follows the preview's rules — a list of root-relative nonblank path strings (an empty list is allowed), each resolved like a plan input path so absolute or symlink-escaping paths raise `ValueError`, matched by resolved path only: files need not exist and are never read, duplicates, aliases and argument order change nothing, and a legal path matching no task input produces no targets. Execution order, failure records and `blocked_by` propagation are `run_plan`'s: input read failures, unknown operations and invalid contents are recorded `failed` with their error, independent branches keep running, blocked tasks never read their input, `blocked_by` lists every failed or blocked direct dependency in declaration order, and dependency decisions use only this run's results. The returned list holds this run's records in actual processing order and the report at `output` contains exactly those records under `results`, replacing any prior content; tasks outside the scope are not read, produce no records and cannot affect the exit code, and the CLI counts describe that same scope with the usual summary fields and exit codes (0 when nothing failed or blocked, otherwise 1). With no changed inputs or no matching task `run_changes` returns `[]` without reading task inputs, creating directories or rewriting the report, and the CLI prints `{"completed":0,"failed":0}` and exits 0. The whole plan — names, dependencies, every input path and output protection, including unselected branches and an empty scope — is validated before the scope is chosen; any violation or an illegal `changed_inputs` raises `ValueError`, and the CLI prints error-only JSON and exits 2 without running tasks or changing files. Saving follows the atomic report-saving rule: an unencodable report raises `ValueError` and filesystem errors raise `OSError` (CLI: error-only JSON, exit 2) after tasks have run, leaving the pre-run output byte-for-byte intact, and executed tasks are not undone. `--run-changed` cannot be combined with `--only`, `--preview`, `--retry-preview`, `--retry`, `--compare`, `--explain`, `--history` or `--changed`.

To record why a run happened alongside its results, pass `record_reasons=True` to `run_plan`, `run_retry`, `run_history_retry` or `run_changes`, or add the CLI flag `--record-reasons`. The option defaults to off: with it absent or false every report, returned list, CLI summary line and exit code is exactly as before. When it is on and the run processes at least one task, the report written to `output` gains one extra top-level field — `execution` — while `results`, the returned list, the CLI statistics and the exit code are unchanged; only `output` is ever written (no extra files or directories, no timestamps). `execution` is an object with exactly `mode`, `targets` and `jobs`. `mode` is `"all"` for an unfiltered plan run, `"only"` for an explicit `targets`/`--only` selection (even when that selection names every job), `"retry"` for a report-derived retry and `"changes"` for a changed-input run. `targets` lists this run's targets in current plan order: every plan job for `all`, the explicitly named jobs for `only`, the old report's `failed`/`blocked` jobs for `retry`, and the directly changed tasks plus every downstream dependent for `changes`. `jobs` uses the fields and semantics of the matching public preview — the `preview_plan` entries for ordinary runs (`all` reasons and empty `required_by` for a full run, otherwise `target`/`prerequisite`), `preview_retry` (or `preview_history_retry` for a history range) for retries and `preview_changes` (including `triggered_by`) for change runs — with the same job names, in the same order, as the run's `results`. Shared prerequisites therefore appear exactly once; failed and blocked jobs keep the selection reasons their preview assigned them and the reasons are never rewritten from this run's outcomes. With no retry targets or no changed-input match the run still returns `[]`, writes no report and creates no directory even with the option on. For a retry whose `report` equals `output`, the reasons come from the report content read before the overwrite; target ordering, changed-path ordering and aliases of the same file follow the existing preview rules and cannot change the recorded reasons. `record_reasons` must be a plain boolean — any other value (including `0` or `1`) raises `ValueError`; the CLI's `--record-reasons` cannot be combined with `--preview`, `--retry-preview`, `--changed`, `--compare`, `--explain` or `--history` (the CLI prints error-only JSON and exits 2). Reports carrying `execution` need no migration: every report reader (`preview_retry`, `run_retry`, `compare_reports`, `explain_report`, `query_history`, `preview_history_retry`, `run_history_retry`) treats it as an ignored extra field under the usual extra-field rules, and a later run without the flag writes a report without it again.

To read back why a recorded run happened, call `query_execution(root, jobs, output, report)` or pass `--execution REPORT` (with the usual plan argument, `--root` and `--output`). It returns an object with only an `execution` field: the report's recorded `execution` — `mode`, `targets` and `jobs` — reduced to the published reason fields (each job keeps only `name`, `depends_on`, `reason` and `required_by`, plus `triggered_by` for `changes` mode), with every array in the order the report recorded and every value preserved as recorded — the historical selection is never recomputed, and failed or blocked records do not rewrite reasons. A report without an `execution` field (written before reasons could be recorded, or with the option off) and a report with empty `results` both return `{"execution": null}`. Validation mirrors `compare_reports` first: the whole plan, every input path and the output path are checked, and the report's `results` must satisfy the compare report's strict path, encoding, structure, name, status and payload rules, so a partial report is legal. The whole file is strict JSON, so a bare `NaN`/`Infinity`/`-Infinity` constant rejects the query anywhere it appears — nested in a `result`, in a record's or top-level extra field, or inside `execution` (including its own extra fields) — even when `results` is empty, no `execution` is present or the query would otherwise return `null`; the same words inside strings are harmless. A present `execution` must then be an object whose `mode` is one of `all`/`only`/`retry`/`changes`, whose `targets` is a nonempty duplicate-free list of current plan job names, and whose `jobs` is a nonempty list of objects matching `results` in name and order and covering every target; each job's `depends_on` must equal the current declaration, `required_by` (and `triggered_by`, required in `changes` mode) may reference only targets, and no task-name list may repeat. For `all` the targets must cover the whole plan and every job needs reason `all` with an empty `required_by`; otherwise each job's reason must be `target` or `prerequisite` according to whether it is a target. Beyond types, references and these correspondences the recorded reason lists are trusted as-is. Missing fields, wrong types, unknown references, an illegal mode, a broken correspondence or an `execution` that is `null` all raise `ValueError`; extra fields are ignored. `--execution` cannot be combined with `--only`, `--record-reasons` or any other execution, preview or report-query option; the CLI prints error-only JSON and exits 2 on any validation failure or conflict, while a valid query exits 0. The query is strictly read-only — it reads only the plan and the named report (`report` may equal `output`), never task inputs, and it never runs tasks, creates directories or writes files.

The API is `execute_job(root, job)`, `run_plan(root, jobs, output, targets=None, record_reasons=False)`, `run_retry(root, jobs, output, report, record_reasons=False)`, `run_history_retry(root, jobs, output, reports, record_reasons=False)`, `run_changes(root, jobs, output, changed_inputs, record_reasons=False)`, `preview_plan(root, jobs, output, targets=None)`, `preview_retry(root, jobs, output, report)`, `preview_history_retry(root, jobs, output, reports, max_failures=None)`, `preview_changes(root, jobs, output, changed_inputs)`, `compare_reports(root, jobs, output, before, after)`, `explain_report(root, jobs, output, report)`, `query_history(root, jobs, output, reports, targets=None)` and `query_execution(root, jobs, output, report)`. `preview_plan` takes the same arguments as `run_plan` and returns `{"jobs": [...]}` without running anything: it never reads job inputs, creates directories, writes the report or reads an old report, so missing input files, unknown operations and invalid file contents do not fail a preview (it does not promise the tasks would succeed). The jobs array covers the selected targets and every prerequisite — shared prerequisites appear once, independent branches are omitted — in the same order the run would process them. Each entry has only `name`, `depends_on` (declaration order, `[]` when omitted), `reason` and `required_by`: without targets every reason is `all` and `required_by` is `[]`; with targets explicit targets are `target` (even when they are also prerequisites of another target) and every other included job is `prerequisite`. `required_by` lists the explicit targets that need the job directly or indirectly, including a job that is itself a target, in original plan order without repeats, so swapping target arguments leaves the preview unchanged. The whole plan is still validated first — names, dependencies and every input path, including unselected branches — and the output path is checked against the root boundary, task inputs and (in the CLI) the plan file; any failure or illegal target raises `ValueError`, the CLI prints its `{"error": ...}` JSON, returns 2 and leaves existing reports untouched. The CLI flags `--preview` and `--retry-preview` print those objects and return 0 instead of executing; `--retry` performs the execution described above. Without any retry or preview option all run behavior, records, ordering, blocking, `--only` scoping, summary fields and exit codes are unchanged. `execute_job` keeps its original semantics and knows nothing about dependencies. All input, plan and report paths must be relative and resolve inside root, including symlinks; the pre-run input path checks apply to blocked jobs too. Reports cannot replace a job input; the CLI also protects its plan. Operations are implemented directly in Python: no shell commands, subprocess execution, schedules, timestamps or automatic retries are available — a retry happens only when requested manually. Only the current run's results drive dependency decisions; `run_retry` reads the historical report solely to choose its targets, never to inherit records. This is a local trusted-user utility rather than an OS sandbox; it does not isolate concurrent filesystem changes.

Run `python3 -B -m unittest -v` for deterministic outputs, failure records, path boundaries, symlinks and CLI validation.

sources); every other execution, preview or query option conflicts.

python3 job_planner.py samples/plan-dependencies.json --compare .results/deps.json .results/deps.json
Reads two reports without running anything and prints {"jobs": [...]}, one
entry per task recorded in either report in plan order, each with name,
before, after (null on the missing side; otherwise just status plus
result/error/blocked_by) and change: added, removed, changed or unchanged.
Status or payload differences count (including error text); result compares
as JSON (true is not 1, a number is not the same digits in a string,
object key order is ignored, array order matters) and numbers nested in
result compare by their exact decimal value without float precision loss
(1, 1.0 and 1e0 are equal, as are 1e400 and 10e399 and -0 and 0, while
0.10000000000000001 vs 0.1, 9007199254740992.0 vs 9007199254740993.0,
1e400 vs 2e400 and 1e-400 vs 0 differ); both sides keep the original
numeric value as a JSON number and blocked_by compares as a set and
prints in current dependency order. Both paths may be the same file.
A valid comparison exits 0 even with failed records; bad reports/
payloads, escaping paths or a bad plan exit 2 with an error JSON —
NaN, Infinity and -Infinity reject a report even in ignored extra
fields, though long decimals and legal exponents beyond float range are
fine. Nothing is created or written. Cannot combine with --only,
--preview, --retry-preview or --retry.

Explain
python3 job_planner.py samples/plan-dependencies.json --explain .results/deps.json --output .results/deps.json
Reads one report without running anything and prints {"jobs": [...]}, one
entry per failed/blocked task in plan order, each with name, status and
causes. A failed task's cause is itself with its error string; a blocked
task follows the report's blocked_by chains to terminal failed tasks or to
unrecorded tasks ({"status": "unrecorded", "error": null}), deduplicated by
name and ordered by the plan. Nothing is inferred from current files or
other declared dependencies; a blocked_by chain reaching a completed record
exits 2 with an error JSON. Partial reports are valid and unrecorded tasks
appear only as trace endpoints; no failures print {"jobs": []}. Report
validation, paths and output protection match --compare; report may equal
--output. A valid explanation exits 0 even with failed records; bad
reports, escaping paths or a bad plan exit 2 with an error JSON. Nothing is
read besides the plan and report and nothing is created or written. Cannot
combine with --only, --preview, --retry-preview, --retry or --compare.

Change preview
python3 job_planner.py samples/plan-dependencies.json --changed samples/notes.txt
Prints {"targets": [...], "jobs": [...]} for the tasks whose resolved input
path changed plus every downstream dependent (targets, in plan order) and
those targets plus all prerequisites (jobs, in run order, with the --preview
fields plus triggered_by: the directly changed tasks reaching each job, or
[] for prerequisite-only jobs). Repeat --changed for more paths; paths
resolve like plan inputs (absolute or escaping paths exit 2), need not
exist and are never read, and duplicates or argument order change nothing.
No match prints {"targets": [], "jobs": []} and still exits 0. The whole
plan is validated first; failures exit 2 with an error JSON. Nothing runs
or is written. Cannot combine with --only, --preview, --retry-preview,
--retry, --compare, --explain or --history.

Run changes
python3 job_planner.py samples/plan-dependencies.json --run-changed samples/notes.txt
Executes the same scope the change preview would show for the same paths:
directly changed tasks plus every downstream dependent (targets) and all
their prerequisites, shared once. Repeat --run-changed for more paths;
paths resolve like plan inputs (absolute or escaping paths exit 2), need
not exist and are never read, and duplicates or argument order change
nothing. Ordering, failures and blocked_by follow a normal run, judged on
this run's results only; the report at --output holds just this run's
records and out-of-scope tasks are never read or recorded. No match (or
no paths) prints {"completed":0,"failed":0}, exits 0 and touches no
files. The whole plan is validated first; failures exit 2 with an error
JSON, and save failures exit 2 with an error-only JSON and no statistics,
keep the previous report byte-for-byte (or absent) and do not undo
finished tasks.
Cannot combine with --only, --preview, --retry-preview, --retry,
--compare, --explain, --history or --changed.

Record reasons
python3 job_planner.py samples/plan-dependencies.json --record-reasons
Adds an optional record of why the run happened: the report at --output
gains one top-level "execution" object (only when at least one task
runs), with exactly mode, targets and jobs. mode is all for a full run,
only for --only selections (even selecting every job), retry for
--retry and --run-history-retry, and changes for --run-changed. targets are this run's targets
in plan order: every job, the explicit targets, the old report's
failed/blocked jobs, or the directly changed tasks plus their
downstream dependants. jobs use the corresponding preview's fields and
semantics (--preview, --retry-preview or --changed), one entry per
processed job in the same names and order as results, shared
prerequisites once; failed and blocked jobs keep their selection
reasons and results never rewrite them. With --retry onto the same
file, reasons come from the pre-overwrite content. results, the printed
counts and the exit code are unchanged and nothing but --output is
written; no retry targets or no changed match still writes no report
and creates no directory. The API option record_reasons accepts only a
boolean, and --record-reasons cannot be combined with --preview,
--retry-preview, --changed, --compare, --explain or --history (error
JSON, exit 2). Existing readers ignore execution as an extra field and
old reports need no changes.

Report saving
Every run mode saves atomically: the new report is fully serialized and
UTF-8 encoded first, then staged and moved over --output in one replace.
A report that cannot be encoded as one complete UTF-8 JSON document fails
with an error JSON and exit 2 before the filesystem is touched; a
filesystem error while creating the directory, saving the content or
replacing the output (including --output already being a directory) also
exits 2 with an error-only JSON and no statistics. Either way the previous
report keeps its exact bytes — or stays absent when there was none — no
partial or extra files remain (empty new parent directories may), and
finished tasks are not rolled back. Only a successful save replaces the
old report, so a historical report that is also --output stays queryable
after a failed save; an in-root symlink output updates the resolved
target and keeps the link.

    """Validate the failure limit: only None or a positive non-bool integer."""
    if max_failures is None:
        return None
    if (isinstance(max_failures, bool) or not isinstance(max_failures, int)
            or max_failures < 1):
        raise ValueError("max_failures must be None or a positive integer")
    return max_failures


def _history_retry_filter(jobs, deps_by_name, candidates, candidate_sources,
                          counts, max_failures):
    """Apply the failure limit to preview candidates, sharing the rule.

    ``candidates``/``candidate_sources`` come from ``_history_retry_scan`` in
    plan order and ``counts`` is its failure tally. With the limit off every
    candidate is retained; otherwise a candidate is excluded when its own
    count or the count of any direct or indirect prerequisite has reached
    the limit. Returns ``(targets, sources, excluded)`` in plan order, where
    each excluded entry has only ``name``, ``failures`` and ``limited_by``
    (every task at the limit inside the candidate's closure, in plan order
    without repeats). Shared by ``preview_history_retry`` and
    ``run_history_retry`` so both always keep the same range for the same
    input; the limit filters candidates only and never adds prerequisites
    beyond the retained targets' usual closure.
    """
    if max_failures is None:
        return list(candidates), list(candidate_sources), []
    plan_order = [job["name"] for job in jobs]
    targets = []
    sources = []
    excluded = []
    for candidate, source in zip(candidates, candidate_sources):
        closure = {candidate}
        stack = [candidate]
        while stack:
            node = stack.pop()
            for dep in deps_by_name[node]:

def _history_retry_scan(root, jobs, deps_by_name, reports):
    """Validate ``reports`` and return ``(targets, sources, failure_counts)``.

    Reports are read strictly in the given order (repeats keep separate
    positions) and each task is judged by the last report recording it — a
    later report missing the task never clears an older status. Targets are
    the tasks whose latest record is ``failed`` or ``blocked``, in current
    plan order; sources parallels targets with each target's latest status,
    report path and zero-based report index. ``failure_counts`` maps every
    plan task to its number of ``failed`` records since its latest
    ``completed`` record: ``completed`` resets the count to zero while
    ``blocked`` and missing records neither increment nor reset it, and a
    repeated report path counts once per position. Every report is fully
    validated, including out-of-scope and overridden records.
    """
    if not isinstance(reports, list) or not reports:
        raise ValueError("reports must be a nonempty list of report paths")
    if any(not isinstance(report, str) or not report.strip() for report in reports):
        raise ValueError("report paths must be nonblank strings")
    latest = {}
    counts = {job["name"]: 0 for job in jobs}
    for index, report in enumerate(reports):
        records = _read_compare_report(root, report, deps_by_name,
                                       exact_numbers=True)
        for name, record in records.items():
            latest[name] = {"status": record["status"],
                            "report": report, "index": index}
            if record["status"] == "failed":
                counts[name] += 1
            elif record["status"] == "completed":
                counts[name] = 0
    targets = []
    sources = []
    for job in jobs:
        source = latest.get(job["name"])
        if source is not None and source["status"] in ("failed", "blocked"):
            targets.append(job["name"])
            sources.append({"name": job["name"], "status": source["status"],
                            "report": source["report"], "index": source["index"]})
    return targets, sources, counts

def run_history_retry(root, jobs, output, reports, record_reasons=False,

    """Execute a manual retry range derived from several historical reports.

    Target selection and scope mirror ``preview_history_retry`` with the
    same arguments: ``reports`` is a nonempty list of nonblank

    given (repeats keep separate positions and nothing is sorted or
    scanned), each task is judged by the last report recording it — a
    later report missing the task never clears an older status — and tasks
    whose latest record is ``failed`` or ``blocked`` become candidates in
    current plan order. With ``max_failures=None`` (the default) every
    candidate is a target; with a positive, non-boolean integer limit the
    same failure counting and exclusion rule as
    ``preview_history_retry`` applies — a candidate is dropped when its
    own count, or the count of any direct or indirect prerequisite, has
    reached the limit — so the retained targets, their prerequisites and
    their order are exactly what the matching preview lists. The run
    covers the retained targets plus every direct and indirect
    prerequisite — prerequisites the history marked ``completed`` or
    never recorded are re-executed too, and shared prerequisites run once;
    excluded candidates, unrelated branches and every other out-of-scope
    task are neither read nor recorded.

    Execution order, failure records and ``blocked_by`` propagation are
    exactly ``run_plan``'s, driven solely by this run's results: input read
    failures, unknown operations and invalid contents are recorded
    ``failed``, independent branches keep running and blocked tasks never
    read their input. The returned list holds only this run's records in
    actual processing order and is written to ``output`` under ``results``,
    replacing any prior content — old records are never copied. A report
    path may equal ``output`` or name the same file another way; the range
    is chosen from all the historical content read before the overwrite, so
    when ``output`` itself is one of the reports the scope and reasons
    reflect that pre-overwrite content.

    With no retained targets the empty list is returned without reading
    task inputs, creating directories or touching the report — whether no
    candidate existed or the limit excluded every one. The whole plan
    (including unselected branches and an empty scope), every input path
    and the output path are validated first, and then every report is
    fully validated under ``preview_history_retry``'s path, UTF-8,
    structure, name, status and strict payload rules — including
    out-of-scope, excluded and overridden older records — so an illegal
    ``max_failures``, ``reports``, plan or report raises ValueError before
    anything runs and no file changes. Saving follows ``run_plan``'s
    atomic rule: an unencodable report raises ValueError and a filesystem
    error while creating the output directory, saving the content or
    replacing the output raises OSError, in both cases after tasks have
    run, with the pre-run output file preserved byte-for-byte (or still
    absent when there was none), no partial or extra files left behind
    and executed tasks not undone — so a historical report aliasing
    ``output`` stays queryable after a failed save, and only a successful
    save replaces it with this run's results.

    With ``record_reasons=True`` and at least one target, the written
    report additionally carries the top-level ``execution`` object with
    ``mode`` ``"retry"``; ``targets`` and ``jobs`` correspond exactly to
    the filtered ``preview_history_retry`` result (``sources`` and
    ``excluded`` are not recorded), in the same names and order as
    ``results``, computed from the report contents read before any
    overwrite, and the reasons query reads them back without any extra
    fields. With no targets nothing is written and no ``execution`` is
    recorded. ``record_reasons`` must be a bool and ``max_failures`` must
    be None or a positive, non-boolean integer; other values raise
    ValueError.
    """

    _require_bool(record_reasons)
    deps_by_name, report_path = _validate_plan(root, jobs, output)
    candidates, candidate_sources, counts = _history_retry_scan(
        root, jobs, deps_by_name, reports)

        jobs, deps_by_name, candidates, candidate_sources, counts,
        max_failures)
    if not targets:

    selected = _select_jobs(jobs, targets)
    execution = ({"mode": "retry", "targets": list(targets),
                  "jobs": _preview_entries(jobs, deps_by_name, targets)}
                 if record_reasons else None)
    return _run_selected(root, selected, deps_by_name, report_path, execution)

Reports are interpreted strictly in the order given — nothing is sorted by name or modification time and no other reports are scanned — so a repeated path yields a separate, later position. Each task is judged by the last report (highest index) containing a record of it: a newer report that omits the task never clears an older status. A task becomes a retry target exactly when its latest record is `failed` or `blocked`, and targets appear in current plan order regardless of report record order; a task whose latest record is `completed`, or that no report ever records, is not a target. The returned object has exactly `targets`, `jobs` and `sources`. `jobs` cover the targets and every direct and indirect prerequisite — prerequisites that completed in history or were never recorded are included too, shared prerequisites appear once and unrelated branches are omitted — with the same fields, processing order and `target`/`prerequisite` reasons as `preview_plan` with those targets. `sources` corresponds to `targets` one to one and in the same order; each entry has only `name` (the target), `status` (its latest status), `report` (the source path verbatim) and `index` (that report's zero-based position in `reports`). With no targets the result is `{"targets": [], "jobs": [], "sources": []}`. The history only selects the range: the new run's dependency decisions still use only that run's own results, never inherited records. content.text:
Done. The failure limit that previously only narrowed `preview_history_retry` now drives `run_history_retry` with identical scope semantics.

## Changes

**`job_planner.py`**
- Extracted the limit logic into a shared `_history_retry_filter(...)` helper; both `preview_history_retry` and `run_history_retry` now run `_history_retry_scan` + the same filter, so targets, scope and order can never drift. Removed the now-redundant `_history_retry_targets` wrapper.
- `run_history_retry(root, jobs, output, reports, record_reasons=False, max_failures=None)`: validates `max_failures` as `None` or a positive non-bool integer (`ValueError` otherwise), filters candidates by the same failure-count / completed-reset / repeat-per-position / prerequisite-at-limit rules, then runs only retained targets + all prerequisites (shared once). Excluded and out-of-scope tasks are never read or recorded.
